rows: The applied modifications led to reduced shrinkage, excellent adhesion to work platforms and reduced material density, which means that the printed elements are slightly lighter than their counterparts made with standard ABS.
Create aramid fibre reinforced 3D prints that are lighter, more resistant, and easier to print compared to native ABS, thank to Nanovia ABS AF.
Lighter prints compared to native ABS
Higher mechanical resistances compared to native ABS
Increased resistance to friction and shocks
For an outdoor usage, we recommend that you paint your print or submit them to an anti UV treatment, such as our Nanovia smoothing solution.
Aramdid fibers and ABS are sensitive to UV radiation.
Thanks to the aramid fibers Nanovia ABS AF allows for excellent 3D printing properties with limited warping and a great bed adhesion.
Low warping when printing (even less than with carbon fiber composites)
A less abrasive fiber compared to carbon and glass
Whilst printing ABS produces a VOC derivative of styrene.

INEOS Styrolution's sheet for Terluran GP-22 (R-INEOS-TERLURAN-GP22-TDS), a general-purpose ABS injection-moulding grade, prints a density of 1040 kg/m³ (ISO 1183) and a water absorption of 1 % saturated at 23 °C and 0.22 % at equilibrium at 23 °C / 50 % RH (ISO 62), p. 2. The Cambridge Materials Data Book (R-CUED-MATERIALS-DATA-BOOK-2003, SHA-256 2bcf739fd66f...) gives ABS 1.01-1.21 Mg/m³.
